owner: The owner starts development by opening Codex CLI in a local Herdr window, sets product needs and priorities, decides product experience tradeoffs and evaluates demonstrated results. The owner decides matters reserved for their authorization. The owner is building ScopeHub for their own long-term use, whether or not others adopt it.
development_ai: In this owner's current workflow, AI agents fill every engineering role, including requirement synthesis, technical planning, implementation, independent review, coordination, verification, maintenance and handoff of verified results.

Choose algorithms, libraries, internal boundaries and technical architecture autonomously within authorized product, resource and safety constraints; record consequential decisions and inspect existing code.
Convert nearby requirements into observable slices; investigate consequential uncertainty early and keep independent work moving while questions are pending.

During an owner-started session, carry authorized work through implementation, verification and handoff. Continue with the next ready slice while capacity is available. Choose windows, assignments and model roles as needed. Incoming GitHub events do not start a development session. Bring concrete missing inputs or reserved product decisions to the owner.
ask_owner_when: User-visible behavior, product scope or a meaningful experience tradeoff is unresolved and cannot be inferred from accepted requirements.
A change affects user-data retention or irreversible handling, external transmission, costs, runtime authority or an existing explicit permission boundary.

Recommend a paid API, product or service when it would materially improve a concrete development task, even if a workaround exists. Explain the expected benefit, estimated cost and how it is billed. Identify material uncertainties and a viable existing or lower-cost option when available. The owner decides on spending, subscriptions or broader access beyond existing grants.
Publication, merge, release or shared-resource use needs authorization not already granted; preserve existing applicable authorization.
Apply the current source-control authorization in project/delivery.json#/source_control/authorization. Record the owner's subjective product feedback when they actually exercise the program.

During an owner-started session, point out a concrete limitation in personal use, development or maintenance that affects a current task or is likely to impede an upcoming one. One example from the owner's own work can be enough. When others start using ScopeHub, look for specific difficulties such as a setup step that only the owner knows how to complete.

Explain which part of the product or working practice causes the difficulty. Suggest the smallest practical adjustment, preferably one the owner can try and reverse. Explain the tradeoff and how to tell whether it helps. The owner can keep the current practice, try a change or defer it. Record consequential decisions in the existing task or feedback record and revisit deferred advice when new evidence warrants it.
question_protocol: Ask concrete questions about observable behavior and consequences; include a recommended option and the impact of alternatives when useful.
Do not ask the owner to select implementation mechanisms. State technical decisions and their material consequences in proportion to impact.
Clarify the next deliverable, not an exhaustive distant feature inventory. Use examples or a small demonstrable slice when words are insufficient.
Distinguish confirmed requirements, temporary assumptions and unresolved questions. Elapsed time is not an answer or approval.
product_ai_separation: This record governs the project owner and the AI developing ScopeHub. It does not define the behavior of product users or the embedded product AI.
Product AI aims to perform user manual work and competently assist with cognitive work in the financial workbench; concrete capabilities and interactions are refined through delivery.
Development delegation does not grant the embedded AI runtime permissions. Product interaction choices remain unspecified until requirements establish them.

Product user means any individual using ScopeHub. Give each user control of their own local data, model routes and grants. Development privileges and the owner’s personal choices apply only in their respective contexts.

module_design: Group logic by responsibility and reason to change. Keep unrelated capabilities independent; do not introduce an abstraction or service without a concrete use.
Expose narrow operations and stable data contracts. Hide internal classes, vendor SDKs, storage layout and processing details; review every new public entry.
Declare allowed dependencies and avoid cycles. Composition roots assemble implementations; callers use public entries instead of implementation internals.
state_ownership: Assign one logical owner to each mutable business state and invariant; distinguish business authorization from storage execution.
Application use cases authorize and coordinate mutations; domain logic owns domain invariants; persistence executes transactional storage through the core single-writer path.
UI and workers do not write the application database. Cache disposal must preserve accepted user work.
Validate structure at ingress, business preconditions in the owning use case and integrity in storage. Multiple defenses must not create divergent copies of the same business rule.
verification: Protect domain rules with independent examples, module collaboration with contract tests and critical user journeys with actual integrated behavior.

Report the results of the affected checks as soon as they are available. Track protected integration in the background and distinguish its outcome from the demonstrated change and from release acceptance.
Test boundary, failure, cancellation and recovery behavior proportional to risk. Builds and schema validation establish only their own scope.
Keep expected values independent of implementation; do not refresh golden outputs merely to pass. Changed requirements need explicit rationale and revised relevant assertions.
Architecture checks enforce declared imports and dependencies, not complete design quality; inspect the actual diff and behavior.

Use current-contract task dependencies to schedule work. Complete physical Windows experience after integrated Ubuntu Tauri desktop acceptance in M1-012. External-session and packaged-release gates require independent evidence.
evolution: When first choosing a consequential design, compare how well viable options serve the user's workflow now. For a plausible future change, identify which callers and saved user work would need to move and how to verify the result. Count the present cost of extra interfaces or parallel implementations too. A direct implementation can be the best choice even when replacing it later will take work.
For a refactor, replacement, migration or requirement reset, identify preserved and intentionally changed behavior, affected callers, data handling and cleanup before activation.

Make a small reversible change in its owning module and exercise the affected behavior in the current task. For a consequential rewrite, compare adapting the current implementation with replacing it or retiring it if the agreed workflow no longer needs it. Include the work for callers, verification, data conversion, coexistence and retirement. Use a representative example to resolve an assumption that could change the choice.

A direct replacement can retire the old path in the same change when all supported callers can move together and affected state is absent, disposable synthetic data or demonstrably compatible. Check for saved user work even before launch. When a change needs stages, use existing task dependencies and record a working state, affected callers, an exit check and a recovery point for each stage.

Before switching a caller, capture its required behavior at the public entry, including failure cases and old inputs. Compare both implementations on representative read-only fixtures when useful. Keep one authoritative writer while moving mutations and exercise recovery on a copy of existing data.

Move callers in bounded groups and verify each through its normal entry. Keep the previous path only while recovery or a supported consumer needs it. Assign remaining cutover or removal work to a successor task with a concrete trigger. After the last caller and supported data version move, remove the obsolete path, transition switch and redundant checks while retaining coverage of current commitments.

Version persistent formats and test migrations against representative old data before use. Retain failed evidence and verify backup/restore or forward repair; an application rollback does not prove data downgrade safety.

When the agreed outcome changes, update the working requirement, its behavior checks and any unfinished plan. For previously completed work, link a successor task. For a consequential change to an accepted decision, record a superseding ADR so the original rationale remains available.
review: Before completion inspect responsibility cohesion, dependency direction, public surface, business/data ownership, failure cleanup, protected behavior and transition removal.
Review tests for independent expectations and real failure detection. Explain remaining limits and actual owner feedback without inventing product acceptance.

Permission and model-connection changes enter independent review from their existing plan change types. Use plan.evolution.data_effect to distinguish destructive user data changes from preserved data or isolated additions. Unclassified persistence changes enter review. Set plan.independent_review for other consequential work using its evolution and risks. Confirmed major and critical corrections enter review through feedback. Open a scoped re-review with project:review --request before dispatch. An explicit request may replace an earlier source without carrying its decision forward. Retain the final exact-source decision and complete observed prose sentence before accepting the work. Start the final independent response with the disposition, task ID and full reviewed SHA. Give one standalone factual English observation in a plain paragraph, put citations below it and continue the owner explanation in Chinese. Put the exact observed sentence in a UTF-8 file for project:review --observation-file.
Address concrete debt in the current slice or attach a bounded successor task with a trigger; avoid unrelated cleanup and speculative frameworks.
feedback_loop: Read status and focused context; inspect implementation; define one observable result and expose the highest-impact uncertainty.

Treat feedback as evidence for a decision. Separate the observed difficulty and intended outcome from the suggested solution. Experiment when useful, using synthetic data to reproduce the observation and checking proposed changes against the intended outcome. Weigh the evidence and the product priorities. Adopt a change within authorized scope, keep the present design, decline the suggestion or defer the decision. Record consequential findings and the reason for the decision or what would reopen it in the existing task or feedback record.
When verification confirms a violation of an existing requirement, follow the applicable engineering repair policy in project/delivery.json.
Inspect the working interaction and exercise its affected checks. Select additional checks for the coverage they add, correct consequential failures and archive the evidence required by the task.
Separate engineering verification, ready-for-owner-review, observed owner acceptance, integration and release. Report each honestly.
Keep focus, next action and meaningful feedback current. Turn recurring failures into proportionate regressions; remove obsolete rules through reviewed decisions.

modules.responsibility: Cross-language domain types, structural wire validation and bounded declarative indicator evaluation.
owns: Domain vocabulary, wire decoding invariants and declarative indicator calculation semantics
invariants: No UI, database or adapter dependencies

modules.responsibility: Use cases, authorized operation dispatch and market semantic validation.
owns: Operation authorization and cross-field market invariants
Local human text connection grants, current chart-purpose authorization and final recipient projection
invariants: Reject unsupported operations; actor identity comes from trusted transports

Synthetic history reads use explicit sources. Local CSV preview, reviewed mapping and full publication require the trusted desktop human transport and a live file selection. Frozen reads require profile entitlement and use immutable stored data.

modules.responsibility: Controlled worker lifecycle and correlated, bounded transport, including a direct OpenAI Responses connector.
owns: Owned child processes and request lifecycle
Fixed-destination OpenAI Responses HTTPS serialization and output validation
invariants: No mutable adapter escape through the application registry
Shutdown releases owned workers
The OpenAI connector accepts the admitted credential for one account-scoped request and transmits only the bounded conversation projection

modules.responsibility: Tauri application assembly and allowlisted native commands. The current native host targets Windows. M1-031 adds the native Ubuntu host. The Ubuntu browser preview uses a separate development transport.
owns: Window identity and application assembly
Trusted credential entry for the active profile and session-only Ubuntu preview key storage
invariants: Bind user actor at the transport; no general file/process/SQL command
Only a native directory picker supplies the root of a local CSV selection
The local human credential command returns configuration state and lifetime. The core receives only an opaque credential revision.

modules.responsibility: User intent and presentation of verified operation results.
owns: Presentation and current selection
invariants: No provider SDK or database access
Late responses cannot replace newer selections
Apply engineering-contract-v1.json#/ui/design_reference to every desktop screen, panel and application dialog.

modules.responsibility: Hide chart SDK and canvas lifecycle behind chart operations.
owns: Chart resources and rendering
invariants: Dispose resources; preserve market identity and units

modules.responsibility: Validated protocol dispatch for controlled worker roles.
owns: Protocol role and dispatch state
invariants: Protocol-only stdout; no database writes

modules.responsibility: Market-data adapters for synthetic acquisition and bounded local file preview.
owns: Source-specific data and aggregation semantics
invariants: Preserve provenance, trading day and unknown volume
No silent source fallback or application database writes

modules.responsibility: Profile-bound SQLite workspace transactions, committed operation receipts, and versioned migrations.
owns: Physical storage and migrations
Stored reviewed mapping versions and their source header associations
Published local CSV revisions, retained source bytes and display rights
invariants: Use the Rust core single-writer path and preserve accepted versions
Append reviewed mapping versions within the bound profile transaction
Bind each local CSV revision to the accepted mapping, deduplicate original bytes and check display rights on frozen reads

modules.responsibility: Native resources, including Windows workspace ACL admission, read-only access to explicitly selected directories, and profile-owned OpenAI credentials.
owns: OS-specific resources
Native policy and worker containment for Windows workspace storage
Windows current-user credential lifecycle and process-local credential storage for portable sessions
invariants: Credential values remain outside the database and logs. The trusted connector resolves the matching revision within the bound profile and provider namespace.
Local import reads resolve catalog-issued file IDs inside the current native selection

modules.responsibility: Credential-free Ollama text adapter and product collaboration execution.
owns: Ollama text model HTTP adapter
invariants: Send the final core-projected text request to its selected endpoint. Use no ambient credentials, proxy, implicit fallback or stored private data.

modules.responsibility: Declarative computation and explicitly authorized trusted Python.
owns: Calculation state and output semantics
invariants: Failed preview cannot overwrite accepted results

modules.responsibility: Repository validation, views, evidence and recovery.
owns: Development records and verification provenance
invariants: Historical evidence is not current or release acceptance
Control checks remain independently testable

capabilities.boundary: One synthetic chart session can search a China future, a China stock and a US stock, change timeframe and chart style, and compare partial and final worker updates with frozen history. The Data sources panel exposes the selected revision, UTC window, freshness, session, coverage, gaps and worker or transport failures. M1-003 covers recovery after interruption. User-configured feeds and physical Windows experience have separate evidence.
The Rust profile store supports a scoped timeframe change and undo across process restart. Desktop access, private records, backup and complete migration acceptance remain under M2-001.

A local human can run and cancel typed declarative previews on authorized frozen CSV intervals, accept one exact result, restore it under current source rights, and remove or undo its chart attachment. CSV calendar identifiers do not establish a schedule. The ordinary bound synthetic chart re-reads and verifies the displayed snapshot, earlier warm-up and explicit adapter sessions before preview. Trusted Python and accepted synthetic artifacts remain separate slices.

Planned shared evidence, reviewed mappings and visible outcomes. The financial partner challenges a thesis, revises its own conclusion and reviews user-selected decision notes. Replay and observed real-model discussion establish different aspects. Versioned research methods require a dated evidence replay and a missing-input case.
Native compilation is not packaged clean-machine acceptance.

A local CSV folder can be used offline. Ordinary text setup reviews Ollama or OpenAI Responses for the current profile and session. OpenAI uses the explicitly configured API key and named destination. Controlled transport, native Windows use and real account qualification are verified independently. M1-030 covers the independent My data sources settings entry for personal records and directly purchased API connections.
Later research delivery retrieves a permitted original, highlights its evidence, preserves uncertainty and returns to the prior view. Channels are independently replaceable.
Later delivery covers a preset, a documented custom HTTP mapping and a dedicated CTP market-data connection. Each requires actual source and permissions verification.
M1-008 accepted explicit session-scoped CSV import, mapping reuse and reviewed publication. Saved-directory catch-up and typed Parquet sources have separate pending product gates.

The built-in workspace chart, watchlist and inspection panel share a typed, editable definition and profile-local layout store. Registered human and scoped AI edits use the same preview, apply, undo and revision checks. Independent comparison uses the selected simulated catalog. Source restoration uses current profile access. Native Windows and owner review remain separate. Adding or removing widgets and rebinding compatible local or API data across views is planned in M2-012.
V1 requires an original chart-free workbench that users can build, revise, refresh and reopen. M2-013 owns the product journey and the release check. Built-in layout receipts cover the chart default.
Opt-in duplex speech shares text context and core permissions. A real session must be observed separately from mock evaluation.

M2-003 selects a renderer using native evidence about expressiveness, editing, resource use, authority and recovery. Running user-authored code in an isolated renderer is a candidate subject to that decision.
One explicitly configured adapter is observed. Candidate model providers, tool capabilities, routing and voice support are qualified individually.
Local bridge and actual CLI and desktop client observations are pending. Only the user's selected workspace, operations and permitted data enter the external client.
Optional licensed market data and managed AI may be selected independently of user-supplied connections. Service qualification and pricing are outstanding.
Future technical connectivity requires a separately qualified workflow with a user-held account. Customer investment funds and settlement stay with the brokerage or futures firm.
Versioned local storage, per-user isolation, selected excerpts and actual provider egress are verified by their delivery tasks. Development-host permissions apply only to the development work.

improvement_metrics: Measure context characters and relevant source lookups for representative tasks before and after changes.
Track consequential clarification, rework and escaped-defect observations; do not infer accuracy gains from smaller prompts alone.

If similar changes repeatedly touch unrelated callers or require users to fix saved work by hand, record one concrete example in the existing task or feedback. After changing the boundary, use the next comparable change to see whether the extra caller edits or user steps were eliminated.

data_ownership.rule: Authorized, revision-bound mutations through the Rust core single-writer queue.
Acceptance creates immutable versions; previews and cache disposal do not overwrite accepted work.
Source adapters own source semantics and provenance, not application database writes.

An explicit local review appends a mapping version associated with the selected source and its decoded header in the current profile. Resolve a live selection again before reuse. Saving a mapping grants no source access.

Publish only a fully checked source under an active native selection and genuine reviewed mapping. Store source bytes, mapping identity, frozen bars and row locators in the profile. Frozen reads require that profile's display right and never reopen the selected directory.
Own process and correlated request lifecycle; expose explicit shutdown and read-only status.
The UI owns hover, focus, pan, unsaved viewport and current visual intent. Ignore superseded asynchronous reads. Published evidence selection and mutation targets belong to the application.
Adapter creates and disposes chart SDK resources.
Validate definitions and archive observed evidence; preserve accepted history.

The SQLite writer persists the explicitly selected published CSV revision UUID, interval and independent selection token. The application holds the selected verified synthetic snapshot and range in memory against the same token. The Rust registry revalidates current permissions and source rights for each selection or projection. Other target kinds and general bound durable mutations are pending.

The local Rust single writer stores explicitly saved typed exchanges, memories and strategies, and applies corrections, deletion and backup recovery within the bound profile. The core also owns any future retrieval data and excerpt grants. Those behaviors are tracked by their delivery tasks.

Profile-bound in-memory route disclosure, grant and bounded successful ordinary text pairs. An OpenAI grant binds the opaque profile credential revision and supports ordinary conversation text. Changing that revision revokes the OpenAI review or grant. Opted-in Ollama chart turns recheck the current selection and opt-in sample purpose, and dispatch at most one registered read using the embedded AI principal. Chart turns do not enter outbound conversation history. Restart, disconnection, cancellation or a new valid proposal revokes the grant.

The platform writes or removes a current-user Windows Credential Manager entry scoped to the OpenAI provider and trusted profile. The native connector resolves the value only for that profile and the approved revision.

model_selection: Use the implementation profile for code changes and the supervision profile for independent review and coordination. Start each assignment at the first configured reasoning effort.

At launch, resolve the newest stable numeric generation in the selected family that the installed Codex catalog lists with the requested effort. A dry run uses the local catalog snapshot. If no model qualifies, report the requested family and effort so the coordinator can resolve the missing capability.

Choose effort for the correctness risk. Start at high or above when a change touches data migrations, concurrent updates, financial precision or permission boundaries and the risk warrants deeper reasoning. Escalate during follow-up work when a failing regression or a review finding leaves the cause uncertain.

Use --effort for a single assignment. Use --escalate-model when an implementation needs the supervision family to resolve a difficult design or correctness question. State the concrete reason in the assignment. Each new assignment starts from its role default.
Prefer code quality when speed or cost conflicts with correctness. Verify the result with the affected checks and independent review in proportion to risk, including after an escalation.
parallel: Choose a single terminal for a small change. For independent bounded work, open local Herdr tabs and assign each a task, scope, public boundary and the expected check. Choose the supervision profile for coordination or independent review when warranted.

Use separate Git worktrees for overlapping writers or independent test runs. Writers sharing a checkout own disjoint paths. One integrating developer owns shared task state, schema generation, evidence recording and source publication. Verify and reconcile actual diffs at one revision.

Inspect the actual terminal result and tests, recover interrupted work from the ledger, and keep working on ready product slices while other jobs run. Retire only work sessions created for the completed assignment.

Start each assignment in the checkout that owns its paths. Implementation and coordination use Codex automatic approval review with workspace-write. Independent review is read-only and returns a blocked operation directly. Report a denial with the requested action and reason to the coordinator, and continue other permitted work. Changes in authorization, paid access and product acceptance stay with the owner.
tooling: For authorized work on this repository, the development AI may independently select, install and configure development tools within existing access and spending grants. These include build and test tools, command-line utilities, skills, MCP servers and plugins. Use trusted distributions and the pinned project setup where applicable. Test the capability before relying on it.

Keep development tools scoped to project code and synthetic fixtures. Use the product user’s chosen grants and data policy independently. Escalate an actual missing credential, entitlement, device, input, product tradeoff or required acceptance with the concrete action needed.

A visible implementation or source-bound review launched by a matching local Herdr parent on supported Linux registers automatically. Use --parent to specify an exact local parent, or --standalone for a deliberately interactive session. Previously started or unregistered tabs are not adopted.

From the local coordinator, use pnpm project:herdr <task> implement --assignment "<scope>" --space <space>. Use review with --source <full-clean-commit> for independent review. Select --effort ultra --tier priority for a specific Sol Ultra Fast assignment and --tier default for Astra Standard.

Use the public dry run to inspect launch arguments. When the launcher inherits the parent and automatically manages the assignment, managed_argv shows the registered launch and argv remains the legacy standalone plan. For managed dispatch, call the same project:herdr entry without --dry-run and consume its JSON assignment and terminal IDs. Running a planned hc argv directly does not create an owned lifecycle record.

Inspect with pnpm project:herdr collect --parent <terminal> --dry-run. Recover with pnpm project:herdr collect --parent <terminal> [--assignment-id <id>]. Resume with pnpm project:herdr collect --parent <terminal> --assignment-id <id> --watch.

Use one registered initial CLI turn. For reusable sessions a detached, per-assignment watcher observes completion for up to 24 hours even when no new launch follows. Reusable sessions stay open after archival. A later top-level turn, missing or ambiguous proof, an unrelated foreground program or active dependent terminals may hold that lane. Add --one-shot for a visible owned implementation that runs one noninteractive Codex turn and exits after persisting its verified return. A one-shot runner with a verified terminal and a failed or ambiguous return stays open for inspection.

Use the managed launch assignment ID with collect --assignment-id to recover the private original, completion event and receipt after archival. State lives under XDG_STATE_HOME or ~/.local/state, or the launch --state-dir override. The original Codex rollout remains in its sessions directory. Older archives contain the completion digest in the receipt. Use project:review separately to accept a source-bound review.

Managed collection targets a local Linux Herdr Core Unix socket with readable procfs descriptors and supported Codex CLI rollouts. The baseline is Core 0.1.22, App 0.1.18 and Codex CLI 0.172.0. Collection never sends native kill, removal or desktop close operations. The desktop may remove a one-shot tab after its owned program exits. Collect reports one_shot_tab_closed only after observing a normal exit of the exact registered program and the disappearance of its exact desktop tab and pane. The finished Core row may remain as evidence. macOS, Windows, remote cores, and legacy Herdr TUI are outside managed collection.

implementation_instructions: Start with the M0 foundation. Implement work in task dependency order. Milestones group acceptance and do not require closing a whole earlier group before starting an eligible task. Follow the owner-approved Ubuntu and physical Windows experience sequence.

Edit canonical wire schemas in contracts/schemas/protocol.schema.json; generate language types and operation schema projections with pnpm generate. This engineering file defines product and engineering requirements, not generated schemas.
All dynamic operations must pass through the Rust registry first; do not add generic execute/shell/sql tools
Keep mock implementations until a provider is confirmed; do not temporarily scrape market data from the internet to pretend that integration exists
Implement the native Ubuntu development host and the Windows v1 release. Reserve other host integrations for a separately approved platform scope.
Tests cover protocols, identity, permissions, and computation semantics first, then the UI
Do not implement live trading types, buttons, or tools as hidden placeholders
State explicitly in the final report whether real data and cloud models are configured; do not exaggerate the completed scope
